notable_absence.finding: Every remediation in both tables is either 'copy the missing file to the right place' or 'inspect with openssl and recreate if necessary' - the page never distinguishes an error an administrator can fix without regenerating any certificate (e.g. a permissions fix) from one that forces a full chain regeneration (e.g. an expired root). Coupled with the two sibling pages' finding that this corpus has no per-certificate revocation mechanism at all, this page shows the practical consequence: several of its own listed errors ('Certificate is not valid at this time', SAN mismatches) have 'create a new certificate' as their only offered remedy, with no lighter-weight alternative documented anywhere in the batch.

cross_component_finding: This page is purely a troubleshooting reference (two tables, no procedures of its own) built entirely from vocabulary defined on the other nine pages in this batch - it mints only one new concept (the chain file's internal structure) and otherwise exists to corroborate cert:trust-store, cert:inbox-directory, cert:subject-alternative-name and cert:private-key relations already asserted elsewhere. This is the round's clearest instance of the hypothesis's second watch-item: a page that mostly reuses rather than mints, and the correct extraction outcome is to say so plainly rather than force new distinctions the page's own content (two flat error tables) does not support.
